topic: Treadmills began as a prison punishment (William Cubitt's treadwheel, 1818)

claims.claim: In 1818 British engineer William Cubitt introduced the prison treadwheel (first at Bury St Edmunds and Brixton).
Cubitt had seen prisoners idle and wanted to keep them busy ('habits of industry').
It was a large wheel with steps; prisoners kept stepping up as it turned, holding a rail.
Prisoners worked it for hours at a time.
Its power was often used to grind grain or pump water.
Some treadwheels powered nothing at all - pure punishment.
Britain abolished penal treadwheels around 1900 (Prison Act 1898; last ones by 1902).
Today people use treadmills for exercise, e.g. paying for a gym.
